blocks.html:
Run your product integration API (the service you build — see the Integration overview) against the legacy Docker Compose stack, so the core rmapi can reach it over mTLS and drive its CRUD and Deploy App callbacks. This page is about iterating on your integration; if you want to hack on the core itself, see Set up your dev environment (Docker Compose) in the Develop Deploy App book instead.

Heads up: rmapi here always means the core RASENMAEHER API (pvarki/python-rasenmaeher-api) — the thing you integrate with. The service you ship (e.g. pvarki/python-matrix-rmapi) is a product integration API, never "rmapi".

How your integration plugs into the legacy stack

In docker-rasenmaeher-integration every product integration API runs as its own service that joins two Docker networks and is fronted by a shared nginx (productsnginx). End users and the core never hit your container directly — they reach it at mtls.<product>.<domain> on the product integration APIs port **4626**, and nginx proxies to your service's internal port.

blocks.code:
flowchart LR
    RM["core rmapi\n(user CRUD + Deploy App ops)"] -->|mTLS| PN["productsnginx\n:4626"]
    EUD["End-user device"] -->|"https://mtls.<product>.<domain>:4626"| PN
    PN -->|"proxy_pass"| YOUR["your product integration API\n(internal port, e.g. 8012)"]
    MW["miniwerk"] -->|"issues subdomain + cert\n+ kraftwerk manifest"| YOUR

blocks.html:
miniwerk (the legacy KRAFTWERK emulation) is what gives your service its identity: for each name in MW_PRODUCTS it provisions the <product>.<domain> and mtls.<product>.<domain> certificates and drops a kraftwerk-rasenmaeher-init.json manifest into the product's shared volume (/pvarki/). Your service reads that manifest to learn its own DNS and the core's service-cert CN it must trust. Getting your product into MW_PRODUCTS and onto productsnginx is the subject of Register your integration (Docker Compose) — this page assumes that wiring already exists (it does for the bundled examples like matrixrmapi, takrmapi, blapi).

Prerequisites

  • Docker with Compose v2.
  • The integration repo cloned with submodules (your product lives in its own submodule directory):
git clone --recurse-submodules -j8 git@github.com:pvarki/docker-rasenmaeher-integration.git

If you forgot --recurse-submodules, run git submodule update --init --recursive. On Windows use WSL (not git-bash) and disable line-ending rewriting (git config --global core.eol lf / core.autocrlf false) — see the Set up your dev environment core page for the full Windows notes.

The localhost note (read this before you up)

Local dev uses the domain localmaeher.dev.pvarki.fi, and your integration is reached at mtls.<product>.localmaeher.dev.pvarki.fi:4626. For that to resolve to your machine:

  • Official (OpenDefence-developed) integrations get their localmaeher subdomain resolved to localhost automatically — pvarki DNS already points *.localmaeher.dev.pvarki.fi at 127.0.0.1, so there is nothing to do.
  • If your integration is NOT official, you must make its subdomain resolve to localhost yourself. The simplest fix is an /etc/hosts entry for local dev/testing:

1. Start the local registry

Due to BuildKit cache bugs, the dev compositions push/pull through a local registry on port 5050. Start it once:
docker run -d -p 5050:5000 --restart always --name registry registry:3

2. Pick a composition: rmlocal vs rmdev

The repo provides two compose aliases:

alias rmlocal="PVARKI_DOCKER_REPO=localhost:5050/ docker compose -p rmlocal -f docker-compose-local.yml"
alias rmdev="PVARKI_DOCKER_REPO=localhost:5050/ docker compose -p rmdev -f docker-compose-local.yml -f docker-compose-dev.yml"

• **rmlocal** corresponds best to a real running environment — assets are minified and baked in. Always confirm your integration works under rmlocal before trusting rmdev.
  • **rmdev** layers docker-compose-dev.yml on top: it bind-mounts your source and runs the service under uvicorn --reload so edits are reflected live (this is your inner loop). The bundled docker-compose-dev.yml already does this for takrmapi and blapi; the Matrix example reloads at port 8012 via docker/entrypoint-dev.sh.

Note: to just run the stack with pre-built images (no local build), drop the PVARKI_DOCKER_REPO=localhost:5050/ prefix from the alias.

3. Build and bring it up

Build the init/cert images first (pushing to the local registry), then everything else, then start:

rmdev build takinit miniwerk rmnginx --pull --push
rmdev build --pull
rmdev up

Substitute rmlocal for rmdev for the baked-in composition. OpenLDAP and keycloak-init sometimes fail on first start — just run up again.

Keep only one of rmlocal / rmdev up at a time (running both causes network issues — run down for one first), and use down -v to reset persistent volumes when switching environments. Note down -v deletes certificates and users, so you will re-add everything.

4. Verify your integration answers on 4626

Once the stack is healthy, your service should answer through nginx on the product integration APIs port. A quick health probe (mTLS-protected endpoints will need a client cert; the healthcheck route is open):
curl -k https://mtls.<product>.localmaeher.dev.pvarki.fi:4626/api/v1/healthcheck

If this hangs or fails to resolve, re-check the localhost note above. If it connects but returns 401/403, that is nginx enforcing mTLS — expected for the /api/v1/users/* callbacks the core uses. The internal port your container actually listens on (e.g. 8012 for Matrix) should not be exposed publicly; always go through nginx.

5. Point the core at it and get first-admin access

The core reaches your integration automatically once miniwerk has written the kraftwerk manifest and productsnginx routes to it — there is no separate "point RM at it" step beyond the registration wiring. To exercise the full flow you need an admin; generate the first admin invite code in local mode:
rmlocal exec rmapi -it /bin/bash -c "source /.venv/bin/activate && rasenmaeher_api addcode"

Then open the local UI at https://localmaeher.dev.pvarki.fi:4439, enter the code, choose your admin callsign, and create/approve a user. Each user CRUD event the core processes is mirrored to your integration over mTLS — watch your service logs (rmdev logs -f <yourservice>) to confirm the callbacks land.
